source.title: NCSC Cyber Essentials Requirements for IT Infrastructure v3.2
source.legalReference: Cyber Essentials v3.2 (IASME Consortium, endorsed by NCSC)

strategies.name: Firewalls & Internet Gateways
strategies.description: Boundary protection controls ensuring that internet-facing services are protected by firewalls, email authentication is enforced, and attack surfaces at the network boundary are minimised.

ML1.summary: Establish boundary protection: block legacy authentication protocols, enforce DMARC email authentication, deploy host-based firewall policies, and enable anti-impersonation protection for inbound email.

ML2.summary: Strengthen boundary controls: block access from high-risk countries, deploy attack surface reduction rules to harden endpoints against common attack vectors, and enable Credential Guard to protect authentication secrets.

ML3.summary: Implement advanced boundary hardening: enforce platform-specific conditional access restrictions and control removable storage to prevent data exfiltration via physical media.

strategies.name: Secure Configuration
strategies.description: Controls ensuring that devices and software are configured securely, with unnecessary functionality removed, default passwords changed, and security baselines applied across all endpoint types.

ML1.summary: Deploy device compliance baselines across all platforms (Windows, iOS, Android, macOS), apply CIS security baselines, harden Edge browser, configure Windows Update rings for automated patching, and restrict external SharePoint sharing.

ML2.summary: Harden configurations further: enforce BitLocker full-disk encryption, deploy mobile app protection policies, set default sharing links to internal-only, configure anonymous link expiry, and enable Purview audit logging.

ML3.summary: Implement advanced endpoint hardening: deploy exploit protection, controlled folder access for ransomware prevention, Windows LAPS for local admin password rotation, and restrict device enrollment.

strategies.name: User Access Control
strategies.description: Controls for managing user accounts, enforcing multi-factor authentication, applying least-privilege access, and governing external and guest user access to organisational resources.

ML1.summary: Establish identity foundations: enforce MFA for all users, disable user consent to third-party apps, configure password protection with custom banned lists, enable security defaults, define authentication methods, implement access reviews and PIM.

ML2.summary: Strengthen access controls: enforce risk-based conditional access (sign-in/user risk), require compliant devices, apply location-based restrictions, restrict guest access, deploy phishing-resistant MFA for admins, configure SSPR, and Windows Hello for Business.

ML3.summary: Implement advanced identity controls: enforce device registration MFA, session timeouts for users and admins, platform-specific conditional access, and token protection to bind tokens to specific devices.

strategies.name: Malware Protection
strategies.description: Controls ensuring that anti-malware software is installed, configured, and kept up to date across all devices. Covers endpoint detection and response, real-time protection, and advanced threat prevention.

ML1.summary: Deploy core endpoint protection: enable Defender for Endpoint EDR, configure antivirus real-time protection, deploy next-generation protection policies, and enable Defender AV configuration across Windows endpoints.

ML2.summary: Enhance threat protection: deploy device control policies, configure web content filtering and network protection, enable automated investigation and response, and vulnerability management scanning.

ML3.summary: Implement advanced malware defence: deploy application guard for browser isolation, advanced hunting capabilities, and comprehensive endpoint DLP with insider risk detection.

strategies.name: Secure Management of Services
strategies.description: Controls for securing cloud collaboration services including Teams meetings, SharePoint data protection, email security, and information governance. Ensures services are configured to prevent data leakage and unauthorised access.

ML1.summary: Secure collaboration foundations: disable anonymous meeting join, restrict Teams federation to approved domains, configure meeting lobby for external users, and deploy baseline data classification and DLP policies.

ML2.summary: Strengthen service security: enable meeting lobby for all external users, restrict default presenters to organisers only, block unmanaged device downloads from SharePoint, and deploy eDiscovery hold policies.

ML3.summary: Implement comprehensive service hardening: restrict SharePoint to organisation-only accounts to eliminate anonymous and personal account access.
